security_audit.summary: Most backtick-related static findings are markdown formatting false positives, but several bash examples intentionally run external CLI commands. The main residual risks are sending user-provided TSX and props to inference.sh, shell quoting mistakes when building CLI input, and optional commands that install related skills. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Document that TSX code, props, asset URLs, and render settings are sent to inference.sh. Require user confirmation before rendering sensitive material.
Prefer structured argument handling or a temporary input file instead of embedding user TSX directly inside a single-quoted shell argument.
Move npx skills add examples behind explicit confirmation and warn that they install additional third-party skill content.
Pin installation guidance to a trusted release or checksum-verified installer instead of relying only on a raw branch URL.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Code and Data Submission
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks users to provide React and Remotion TSX code, props, and render settings, then renders them through inference.sh. Sensitive source code, proprietary media URLs, or private data in props could be disclosed to that external service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states that rendering happens via inference.sh and shows TSX code and props being submitted as input. This directly supports a privacy and data-handling risk, although it appears intentional.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Quoting Risk for User-Provided TSX
semantic_findings.description: The CLI examples place large TSX payloads inside single-quoted shell arguments. If an agent inserts untrusted code without robust escaping or a structured input file, shell metacharacters could alter the command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples consistently embed user-controlled TSX and props inside shell-quoted JSON. The file does not show an implementation, so the injection risk depends on how the agent constructs the final command.

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos From React Code
content.value_statement: Teams need fast video previews from React animation code without managing a local Remotion setup. This skill sends TSX to inference.sh and returns rendered MP4 outputs.
actual_capabilities: Renders exported React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 video outputs.
Supports common Remotion APIs including useCurrentFrame, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, and Sequence.
Configures width, height, frame rate, duration, codec, and composition ID.
Passes props into the rendered component for reusable video variants.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows, including streaming progress updates.
limitations: Requires inference.sh access and the belt CLI or Python SDK workflow.
Sends component code, props, and render settings to an external service.
Custom package support depends on the remote Remotion environment.
Render speed and availability depend on inference.sh service capacity.

use_cases.title: Create Launch Videos
use_cases.description: Render short branded announcement clips from reusable Remotion components and campaign text.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Components
use_cases.description: Turn React animation ideas into MP4 previews before adding them to a production video pipeline.

use_cases.title: Publish Data Clips
use_cases.description: Generate animated counters, charts, and explainers for reports or social distribution.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-second Remotion video with a dark background, centered title, fade-in animation, 1920 by 1080, and 30 fps.

prompt_templates.title: Animate Product Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a square video that counts from 0 to 100 and labels the metric as weekly active users. Use five seconds at 60 fps.

prompt_templates.title: Use Props for Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a reusable Remotion component that accepts title, subtitle, and brand color props. Render one MP4 variant for a launch announcement.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sequenced Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10-second Remotion composition with three timed scenes, spring transitions, image placeholders, captions, and streaming progress updates.

output_examples.input: A request for a three-second fade-in title video at 1080p.
output_examples.output: An MP4 render link for a dark title card where the headline smoothly appears over the first second.

output_examples.input: A request to create a square animated counter for a social post.
output_examples.output: A square MP4 render link with a percentage counter, label text, and timing suitable for social feeds.

output_examples.input: A request to stream progress for a longer explainer render.
output_examples.output: Progress updates during rendering followed by a final video link when the job completes.

best_practices: Review TSX, props, and asset URLs before sending them to the remote renderer.
Test with short duration and lower resolution before rendering final video quality.
Use props for titles, colors, and data values to create reusable video variants.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, API keys, private customer data, or proprietary source code into render inputs.
Do not assume arbitrary npm packages are available in the remote render environment.
Do not render untrusted user-provided TSX without review and explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 video outputs through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. Rendering is performed through inference.sh, so inputs are sent outside the local workspace.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I change video size and timing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents width, height, fps, duration, codec, composition ID, and props options.

faq.question: Can it use media assets?
faq.answer: The examples list Remotion media components, but asset access depends on reachable URLs and the remote environment.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. Remove secrets, private data, and proprietary code before sending inputs to the external renderer.
